name: Sweden
summary: Zero-tolerance policy: possessing and even using narcotics is a crime (minor cases: fine or up to 6 months). Many new substances are banned as 'health-hazardous goods'. No drug checking services.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law and drug use is itself a crime. Health staff secrecy rules generally stop them reporting minor drug offences to police, but police may attend.
drugChecking: No drug checking services; there is no legal exemption for testing drugs outside police and forensic labs.

lsd.note: Narcotic. Possession or use (e.g. a positive drug test) is a crime; minor cases get a fine or up to 6 months.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin mushrooms are narcotics. Spores and grow kits are sold, but growing fruiting mushrooms is illegal.

dmt.note: Narcotic; ayahuasca and DMT plant preparations are illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is a narcotic; preparations made from mescaline cacti count as narcotics.

dox.note: DOB, DOM, DOC and similar are classed as narcotics.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT is a narcotic; most other 5-MeO tryptamines are narcotics or banned 'health-hazardous goods'.

cannabis.note: Narcotic; use itself is a crime and police can require drug tests. Medical cannabis only for a few licensed patients.

ketamine.note: Narcotic medicine: possession or use without a prescription is a narcotics offence.

dxm.note: Classed as a narcotic since 2008 (list V); no DXM cough medicines are sold in Sweden.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic. Since 1 July 2025 sales to under-18s or for intoxication are banned; consumers may buy only ≤9 g cartridges, two per sale.

amphetamines.note: Narcotics. ADHD medicines (e.g. lisdexamfetamine, methylphenidate) are legal only with a prescription.

mdma.note: Narcotic; possession or use is a crime.

cocaine.note: Narcotic; possession or use is a crime.

caffeine.note: Legal. No legal age limit on energy drinks; retailers voluntarily refuse sales to under-15s.

alcohol.note: Systembolaget (state monopoly) sells from 20; bars and restaurants from 18; shops sell beer up to 3.5% ABV from 18.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB, GBL and 1,4-BD are classed as narcotics (with industrial exemptions). Sodium oxybate is prescription-only.

opioids.note: Heroin and opioid medicines are narcotics; legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: Classed as a narcotic since 2008: possession without a prescription is a narcotics offence.

benzodiazepines.note: Narcotics: unprescribed possession or use is a narcotics offence. Designer benzos are also classified.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only, not narcotics. Harmala/Syrian rue are not known to be controlled; ayahuasca is illegal (DMT).

ssris.note: Prescription-only, not narcotics: possession isn't a crime, but selling them or importing without permission is.
